These excursions are the dominant morphological feature: they appear as near-vertical drops (duration ≤2 points) followed by instantaneous recovery, forming narrow, deep troughs with amplitude typically between -10 and -11.36 (matching the catalog’s upper/lower extremes). The period of recurrence is approximately 80 points (consistent with estimated_period=80), as seen across candidates 1–3: candidate 1 shows one such event near its end; candidate 2 shows two events spaced ~80 points apart; candidate 3 shows three events spaced ~80 points apart. Noise is negligible—no visible high-frequency jitter or drift outside the steps. Stability is high: baseline remains exactly at 0.0 across all segments except during excursions. No sustained trend is present; slope_per_point is near-zero except in candidate 1 where a slight negative slope appears before the single step, likely due to edge effects or minor contamination. Amplitude is highly consistent across events; peak/trough morphology is uniform—sharp onset, flat bottom (1–2 points), sharp recovery. Acceptable variation includes: (a) number of excursions per window (scaling with window_cycles), (b) exact timing within ±2 points, (c) minor asymmetry in recovery slope. The flat segment (candidate 0) represents a clean, anomaly-free baseline state and is the most reliable reference for nominal behavior.
